title: Risk Sources and Risk Management Measures in Support of Standards for General-Purpose AI Systems

bias_targets.methodology: The paper does not empirically measure this bias itself, but catalogs it as a systemic risk (e.g., in content moderation algorithms objectifying women). It discusses evaluating and mitigating this bias conceptually through algorithm fairness audits, diverse data labeling, and debiasing methods (data pre-processing, objective function interventions during training, and embedding space modifications post-training).

Cataloged as a risk source related to racial stereotypes. Evaluated and mitigated conceptually via diverse data labeling, algorithm fairness audits, and structural debiasing methods applied across the AI development pipeline.

Cataloged as a risk source related to religious stereotypes. Mitigation and evaluation are discussed conceptually via fairness audits and debiasing methods during pre-processing, training, and post-training.
Cataloged as a risk source related to the propagation of dominant ideologies or extremist attitudes. Addressed conceptually through debiasing methods and fairness audits.

Cataloged as a risk source related to the propagation of dominant ideologies. Discussed conceptually in the context of debiasing methods and fairness audits to prevent unintentional bias amplification across communities.
